Import code is included but not rendered below. ::: {.cell} ::: ## Data Cleaning (SPSS) Variable recoding, dummy coding, and composite construction for this project were done in SPSS prior to import into R, across four syntax files by domain (demographics, structural disadvantage, outcomes, protective factors). Each is excerpted below to document the approach. ### Demographics `Demographics.sps` recodes core demographic variables (child sex, age, race/ethnicity) into analysis-ready measures, checking frequencies before and after each recode. ```spss *****************************CHILD SEX. *Q: What is your biological sex? ***check frequencies for zeros. frequencies variables = bio_sex /statistics = all. *male = 1, female = 2. *create dummy code for child biological sex (female = 1). if(bio_sex eq 1) bio_sexD = 0. if(bio_sex eq 2) bio_sexD = 1. variable labels bio_sexD "child biological sex". value labels bio_sexD 0 "male" 1 "female". execute. *check frequencies of new variable. frequencies variables = bio_sexD /statistics = all. ``` ### Structural Disadvantage `Disadvantage.sps` (672 lines) builds individual- and household-level disadvantage indicators, including race/ethnicity dummy codes with missing-data recodes. ```spss *****************************FAMILY SOCIOECONOMIC DISADVANTAGE COMPOSITE. *Components: famincomecat (continuous $, higher = more income), pareduc_avg (0-8, higher = more education), * parentemploy (0-1, higher = more employment). *Standardizing each component to z-score then reverse code so higher is more disadvantage, then average. *standardize based on weight filtered dataset. delete variables Zfamincomecat Zpareduc_avg Zparentemploy. *delete variable if previously standardized with whole sample. temporary. *temporary can't be used with delete. select if (GSWGT3_2 ge 0). descriptives variables = famincomecat pareduc_avg parentemploy /save. *Creates Zfamincomecat, Zpareduc_avg, Zparentemploy. execute. compute Zfamincomecat_r = Zfamincomecat * -1. variable labels Zfamincomecat_r "Family income z-scored reversed (higher = lower income = more disadvantage)". execute. compute Zpareduc_avg_r = Zpareduc_avg * -1. variable labels Zpareduc_avg_r "Average parental education z-scored reversed (higher = less education = more disadvantage)". execute. compute Zparentemploy_r = Zparentemploy * -1. variable labels Zparentemploy_r "Average parental employment z-scored reversed (higher = less employed = more disadvantage)". execute. compute famSES_disadv = mean(Zfamincomecat_r, Zpareduc_avg_r, Zparentemploy_r). variable labels famSES_disadv "Family SES disadvantage composite: mean of z-scored reversed income, education, employment (higher = more disadvantage)". execute. frequencies variables = famSES_disadv /statistics = all. reliability variables = famincomecat pareduc_avg parentemploy /scale('famSES') all /statistics = all. *standardize based on weight filtered dataset. temporary. select if (GSWGT3_2 ge 0). descriptives variables = famSES_disadv /save. *Creates Zfamincomecat, Zpareduc_avg, Zparentemploy. execute. ``` ### Outcomes `Outcomes.sps` (473 lines) constructs the substance-use outcome variable (alcohol, cigarette, and tobacco use composite), depression, general health, and educational attainment. Below is a exert from the final section of scoring the depression outcome. ```spss *****************************CES-D DEPRESSION COMPOSITE (WAVE 3). *9 items (all in same 0-3 direction after reverse coding H3SP7 and H3SP11 above). *Sum score (0-27 range); Desch et al. (2023). compute cesD_sum = sum(dep_bothered, dep_blues, dep_asgood, dep_concentrate, dep_depressed, dep_tired, dep_enjoyed, dep_sad, dep_disliked). variable labels cesD_sum "CES-D depression sum score Wave 3 (0-27, higher = more depressive symptoms)". execute. reliability variables = dep_bothered dep_blues dep_asgood dep_concentrate dep_depressed dep_tired dep_enjoyed dep_sad dep_disliked /scale('CESD') all /statistics = all. frequencies variables = cesD_sum /statistics = all. *standardize based on weight filtered dataset. delete variables ZcesD_sum. *delete variable if previously standardized with whole sample. temporary. *temporary can't be used with delete. select if (GSWGT3_2 ge 0). descriptives variables = cesD_sum / save. ``` ### Protective Factors `Protective.sps` (887 lines) builds the protective-factor composites, several of which are reverse-scored so that higher values consistently indicate greater disadvantage.Below is an example of the data cleaning of one variable and then the creation of one protective factor composite. ```spss *****************************COMMUNITY RESOURCES - CONNECTEDNESS (ADOLESCENT REPORT). *Note: Items reverse-scored here so higher = LOWER community resources (disadvantage direction), *consistent with the structural disadvantage framing of this composite. *Community Connectedness (Wickrama & Bryant 2003): 4 items, yes/no (0/1), summed 0-4. *Reverse scoring: recode 1->0 and 0->1 so high score = LOW connectedness = more disadvantage. if (H1NB1 eq 1) knowneighbR = 0. *knows neighbors = connected (reverse to 0=low disadvantage). if (H1NB1 eq 2) knowneighbR = 1. *doesn't know = disconnected = higher disadvantage. if (H1NB1 eq 6 or H1NB1 eq 8 or H1NB1 eq 9) knowneighbR = -99. recode knowneighbR (-99 = sysmis). variable labels knowneighbR "Does NOT know most neighbors (H1NB1 reversed, 1=low connectedness/more disadvantage)". value labels knowneighbR 0 "knows most neighbors" 1 "does not know most neighbors". execute. *****************************COMMUNITY CONNECTEDNESS INDEX (Wickrama & Bryant 2003). *Items coded in protective direction (1 = connected): *knowneighb, talkneighb, neighbwatch, nbhdsafe. *Sum 0-4; higher = more connectedness = more protective. compute commconnect = sum(knowneighb, talkneighb, neighbwatch, nbhdsafe). variable labels commconnect "Community connectedness (Wickrama & Bryant 2003, sum 0-4, higher = more connectedness)". execute. reliability variables = knowneighb talkneighb neighbwatch nbhdsafe /scale('commconnect') all /statistics = all. *alpha = .51. frequencies variables = commconnect /statistics = all. *standardize based on weight filtered dataset. delete variables Zcommconnect. *delete variable if previously standardized with whole sample. temporary. *temporary can't be used with delete. select if (GSWGT3_2 ge 0). descriptives variables = commconnect / save. ******************************************************************************* ``` The cleaned file was exported and merged into `AddHealth_AllData.sav` for the R analysis above. ## Overview - **Step 0: Create cumulative risk variable.** - Approach: regress each outcome on all individual adversity indicators simultaneously. Extract standardized betas. Use betas as weights to construct an outcome-specific adversity composite. - Citation: Utilize predictor weighting — meaning the contribution of each adversity indicator to the cumulative composite is weighted by its empirical association with the outcome. Marquez et al. (2023) utilized this method; Miller-Lewis et al. (2013) examined bivariate correlations with each outcome and found them all small, so created one composite adversity index. - **Step 1: Regress cumulative risk on outcome** - **Step 2: Extract residuals** - **Step 3: Regress protective factors on residuals** - **Step 4: Repeat step 2-4 with high and low adversity sample split** ## Survey Design Specification Add Health uses a complex, clustered, stratified sampling design. All regressions use the Wave 3 grand sample weight (`GSWGT3_2_2`) via the `survey` package to produce design-consistent estimates. ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: check missing sample weight #how many cases missing cat("Missing GSWGT3_2:", sum(is.na(dat$GSWGT3_2)), "\n") cat("Non-missing GSWGT3_2:", sum(!is.na(dat$GSWGT3_2)), "\n") # ── Subset to respondents with valid Wave 3 weight ──────────────────────────── # Respondents missing GSWGT3_2 were not part of the Wave 3 sample # (e.g., lost to follow-up, deceased, ineligible) and should be excluded dat_w3 <- dat |> filter(!is.na(GSWGT3_2)) ###dat_w3 is name of new dataset for analysis cat("Analytic n after excluding missing weights:", nrow(dat_w3), "\n") # ── Specify survey design on the subsetted data ─────────────────────────────── # Use design_w3 as survey weight design in regressions design_w3 <- svydesign( ids = ~1, weights = ~GSWGT3_2, data = dat_w3 ) cat("Sum of weights:", round(sum(dat_w3$GSWGT3_2), 0), "\n") ``` ```` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Missing GSWGT3_2: 1622 Non-missing GSWGT3_2: 4882 Analytic n after excluding missing weights: 4882 Sum of weights: 22144327 ``` ::: ::: ## Descriptive Statistics ### Code ::: {.cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: create descriptives table # ── Function: get weighted M and SD, and unweighted range ───────────────────── get_desc <- function(var, design) { mn <- as.numeric(svymean(as.formula(paste0("~", var)), design, na.rm = TRUE)) vr <- as.numeric(svyvar(as.formula(paste0("~", var)), design, na.rm = TRUE)) rng <- range(design$variables[[var]], na.rm = TRUE) data.frame( M = formatC(mn, digits = 2, format = "f"), SD = formatC(sqrt(vr), digits = 2, format = "f"), Range = paste0(formatC(rng[1], digits = 2, format = "f"), "–", formatC(rng[2], digits = 2, format = "f")) ) } # Means and standard deviations are weighted using the Wave 3 grand sample weight (GSWGT3_2). Range is unweighted.") |> fontsize(size = 9, part = "footer") |> italic(part = "footer") ``` ```` ::: ## Table: Descriptive Statistics @tbl-descriptives ::: {#tbl-descriptives .cell} ````{.cell-code} ```{{r}} #| label: tbl-descriptives descriptives ``` ```` ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html}
